# Mini guides

Short reads on testing a trading idea without fooling yourself. The web page serves them at `/guides`.

## Before you trust a backtest

- [Five ways a backtest lies](five-ways-a-backtest-lies.md): Quick backtests, especially ones an AI writes in a hurry, are usually too kind. The five common leaks, how to spot each one, and how to close it.
- [Tune settings without finding luck](tune-without-finding-luck.md): Trying settings and keeping the best finds the luckiest one. Hold part of the history back, choose on the rest, and judge once.
- [Write your idea as a rule](write-your-idea-as-a-rule.md): Turn a trading idea into a rule the honest backtester can run, with common setups already translated and every function in one table.
- [Is live keeping the backtest's promise?](live-vs-backtest.md): Live results usually come in below the backtest. How to tell a normal gap from a backtest that was wrong.

## Reading your verdict

- [Why the judge is so strict](why-the-judge-is-strict.md): Most good-looking records are luck. Why "can't tell yet" is the honest answer so often, what it takes to get past it, and why a plain t-test is too easy to fool.
- [Count your versions](count-your-versions.md): The best of many tries looks good by luck alone. How to count what you tried, and how the judge raises the bar to match.
- [Did it just ride the market?](did-it-just-ride-the-market.md): In a rising market, any strategy that buys makes money. How the judge takes the market out, and how rough that is.
- [Broken, or just a bad streak?](broken-or-bad-streak.md): Every strategy has losing runs. How to tell a normal one from a strategy that has stopped working.
